newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse suspends trading in Cofinec.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse suspends trading in Cofinec.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange suspended trading in the Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) of French-registered packaging company Cofinec on Wednesday after excessive intraday falls, a trader told Reuters by phone.
The suspension came at around 1200 GMT after Cofinec GDRs plummeted to 4,250 forints from an opening level of 5,000 forints and Tuesday's close of 5,460 forints.
"It was suspended about a quarter an hour ago, due to too rapid a fall," one trader said.
Wednesday's suspension followed a similar step on Tuesday when trading in Cofinec GDRs was suspended after an unacceptably rapid intraday rise in early trade.
On Tuesday analysts said they saw a link between analysts currently visiting Cofinec plants in Poland and in Hungary and the price surge.
The trader said on Wednesday the price was brought down by a small deal at 4,250 forints/GDR.
This deal followed an agency cross which was concluded for 45,000 shares at 4,650 forints/GDR.
An agency cross is a transaction in which the same brokerage matches a buy and a sell order.
